segments.source: Renewable does not mean unlimited. A resource can decline when use exceeds regeneration.
A forest resource starts at 110 units. Each year it regenerates 18 units and people harvest 18 units. Assume these amounts stay constant for 3 years and no other changes occur.
Annual net change = regeneration − harvest. In this simplified model, use is sustainable over the period if stock does not decline.
What is the stock after 3 years, and is the harvest sustainable under this classroom definition?
1. Annual net change=18−18=0. 2. Three-year change=0. 3. Final stock=110+(0)=110. 4. Compare final stock with starting stock.
110 units; sustainable under the stated definition.
Sustainability is a balance between renewal and extraction over time.
Stock-flow model with regeneration and harvest; test non-decreasing stock.

Problem 171. Population balance in a town: case 1
Population changes through births, deaths, immigration, and emigration.
A town begins the year with 1100 residents. During the year: births=20, deaths=11, people moving in=32, people moving out=25.
End population = start + births − deaths + in-migration − out-migration. Natural change and migration change are separate components.
Compute natural change, migration change, and the year-end population.
1. Natural change=20−11=9. 2. Migration change=32−25=7. 3. Total change=9+7=16. 4. End population=1100+16=1116.
Natural change +9; migration change +7; end population 1116.
Breaking total change into components helps explain why a population grew or shrank.

Compute natural change, migration change, and the year-end population.

Problem 173. Population balance in a town: case 3
Population changes through births, deaths, immigration, and emigration.
A town begins the year with 1200 residents. During the year: births=26, deaths=11, people moving in=32, people moving out=33.
End population = start + births − deaths + in-migration − out-migration. Natural change and migration change are separate components.
Compute natural change, migration change, and the year-end population.
1. Natural change=26−11=15. 2. Migration change=32−33=-1. 3. Total change=15+-1=14. 4. End population=1200+14=1214.
Natural change +15; migration change -1; end population 1214.
